answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce stake before earning fees, then slash it when audits prove that supposedly separate identities share one operator. A sybil farm must fund every account and risk losing that capital; splitting one bond across many names does not meet the per-agent requirement. Auditors can sample behavior from a committed random kernel, catching repeated patterns like a walnut buried in a dune. This raises the cost of fake identities without making them impossible.
